grading_system.evidence: The completion of a minimum of 34 credits is required with the following distribution: English, Math, Science, Global Citizenship, and Electives require six (6) credits in each subject area; Physical Education requires two (2) credits; Health, Visual/Performing Arts require one (1) credit each.

schedule.evidence: Our academic program is organized in a six period schedule with each class being 55 minutes in length. The maximum number of credits per semester is six. Recommended Course Load: fully enrolled throughout the entire school year (6 periods + flex).

credit_definition.text: Maximum 6 credits per semester over six periods, so one semester class = 1 credit (derived from the two stated figures; the catalog does not state a per-course credit value).
credit_definition.evidence: The maximum number of credits per semester is six.

course_load.min_courses_or_credits: fully enrolled throughout the school year (6 periods + flex)
course_load.evidence: Recommended Course Load: The expectation is that students in grade 9-12 will be fully enrolled throughout the entire school year (6 periods + flex).

local_grad_requirements.conversion_note: Catalog credits are the school's own credits; no conversion needed under credit_per_course_term = 1 (one semester class). Distribution: English 6, math 6, science 6, global citizenship 6, electives 6, PE 2, health 1, visual/performing arts 1. Applies to class of 2027 as printed.

flexible_pathways_listed: Vermont dual enrollment (up to two college courses; juniors and seniors)
Vermont early college (senior year at VSU, CCV or Norwich)

notes: Graduation requirements and the schedule statement are on image-only PDF pages (4 and 5), read visually; the phase2 courses JSON's 34-credit block matches. Credit per class is derived (max six credits per semester over six periods), so credit_per_course_term = 1 is inferred, not printed; set to null if the reviewer disallows derivation. Required courses stated in the text: all ninth graders take year-long ninth grade English; all students take Integrated Science 9, Biology and Chemistry; students are expected to take World History I and II and US History before other Global Citizenship courses. Grading moved to a 100-point scale in 2025-26 with unweighted GPA, and transfer, Pass/Fail and flexible-pathway grades are not in GPA. No proficiency-based graduation requirement is stated; the catalog says the 100-point scale keeps 'strengths of standards based learning'. The JSON's 'Schedule: maximum six credits per semester' note is confirmed on PDF page 4. Senior-year early college and dual enrollment details are on text page 7 (printed 6).
